idea.text: meeting-briefer: a small Python portfolio project. A meeting transcript or notes (text file or webhook POST, e.g. from Slack) goes to Claude, which extracts decisions, action items and owners as Pydantic-validated JSON, with retries. A short briefing script is built and spoken with the ElevenLabs text-to-speech API (Norwegian and English). Output: MP3 + JSON summary. FastAPI webhook, eval set of 8 transcripts with a scoring script, logging, .env secrets. Purpose: a job application to ElevenLabs (Internal AI Transformation role). Scope 1-2 days.
idea.summary: A Python service that turns meeting transcripts into validated action-item JSON and a spoken audio briefing, for internal teams, as an API/CLI.
idea.target_user: internal teams who want a short spoken recap of meetings; in practice a portfolio piece for a hiring manager

competitors.name: MoM AI (LLM-Minutes-of-Meeting)
competitors.match_reason: Covers recording or transcript to decisions and action items, LLM choice including Anthropic, logs and metrics, ElevenLabs Scribe for transcription. Missing: spoken TTS briefing, Pydantic-validated JSON with retries, webhook input, eval set, Norwegian.

competitors.name: vtt-summarizer
competitors.match_reason: Transcript file to JSON (overview, decisions, action items) with a second LLM pass to clean the JSON. Missing: Pydantic schema, TTS, webhook, evals.

competitors.name: Meeting-Summary-Generator
competitors.match_reason: Transcript to summary with decisions and action items via OpenAI, .env key. Missing: validated owners, retries, TTS, webhook, evals, Norwegian.

competitors.name: Meetily
competitors.match_reason: Most popular self-hosted meeting assistant: local recording, transcription and summaries. A desktop app with no webhook API and no audio briefing.

competitors.name: Teams-Transcript-Summarizer
competitors.match_reason: Flask app that summarizes Teams transcripts with GPT-4 or Claude-2 into bullets. No owner extraction, no TTS.

competitors.name: Summit
competitors.match_reason: Gemini summaries of Google Meet recordings sent by email. Text only, no structured action items.

competitors.name: Fireflies.ai
competitors.match_reason: Meeting bot with summaries and action items, customizable prompts for owners and deadlines, pushes tasks to other tools. No spoken briefing.

competitors.name: Otter.ai
competitors.match_reason: Notetaker with summaries and assignable action items. Seen only on a third-party comparison page.

competitors.name: Zoom AI Companion
competitors.match_reason: Built-in Zoom summaries with action items, emailed after the meeting. Seen on a university IT page.

competitors.name: meeting-action-items (agent skill)
competitors.match_reason: Prompt-level agent skill for action items.

competitors.name: Vexa
competitors.match_reason: Open-source meeting transcription API, an upstream source of transcripts.

gaps.statement: None of the open-source meeting summarizers found turns the result into a spoken briefing; MoM AI uses ElevenLabs only for speech-to-text.
checked: GitHub search 'audio briefing elevenlabs' (no results above 20 stars)

gaps.statement: None of them ships an eval set that measures extraction quality, so there is no number behind 'it finds the action items'.

building_blocks.name: Anthropic Python SDK
building_blocks.why: Official Claude client; messages.parse returns a validated Pydantic object.
building_blocks.warning: Structured outputs ignore some schema constraints such as string length, so validate the rest yourself.

building_blocks.name: Instructor
building_blocks.why: Pydantic outputs with automatic retries on validation errors.
building_blocks.warning: An extra dependency; a hand-written retry loop shows more of your own work.

building_blocks.name: FastAPI
building_blocks.why: Pydantic request and response models, OpenAPI docs and TestClient for the webhook.

building_blocks.name: pydantic-settings
building_blocks.why: Typed .env loading for the API keys.

building_blocks.name: ElevenLabs Python SDK
building_blocks.why: Official SDK with text_to_speech.convert; the README lists eleven_flash_v2_5 with 32 languages.
building_blocks.warning: GitHub reports no license; PyPI metadata says MIT.

building_blocks.name: VoxCPM2
building_blocks.why: Open local TTS with Norwegian in its language list.
building_blocks.warning: Needs a GPU, and it is a competitor's model in an ElevenLabs application.

building_blocks.name: pytest
building_blocks.why: Unit tests with fake clients, so tests cost no API credits.

building_blocks.name: Pydantic Evals
building_blocks.why: Pydantic-native datasets and evaluators with no server.

building_blocks.name: promptfoo
building_blocks.why: YAML test cases and side-by-side model comparison.
building_blocks.warning: A Node CLI; heavy for 8 transcripts.

building_blocks.name: DeepEval
building_blocks.why: Pytest-style LLM tests with ready-made metrics.
building_blocks.warning: Most metrics use an LLM judge, which adds cost and noise.

building_blocks.name: FastAPI official skill
building_blocks.why: Official FastAPI best practices, Pydantic models, dependencies, async vs sync.

building_blocks.name: ElevenLabs text-to-speech skill
building_blocks.why: Official ElevenLabs TTS usage for Python and JS.
building_blocks.warning: Defaults to eleven_v4; its setup step runs the ElevenLabs CLI, so read it first.

building_blocks.name: Pydantic official skill
building_blocks.why: Model design and constraints for the schema.
